domain: public procurement - pre-award solicitation lifecycle outcome prediction (federal tenders, Canada)
prediction_question: For a Government of Canada competitive solicitation (noticeType in the RFP-like set: Request for Proposal, RFP against Supply Arrangement, Request for Standing Offer, Request for Supply Arrangement, Invitation to Qualify) whose original tender notice is published on CanadaBuys at instant T (publicationDate of the original notice row), will the solicitation be cancelled before award - i.e. its terminal tenderStatus is 'Cancelled' rather than 'Expired'? Features are the original-notice fields fixed at T: title and description text, contracting entity and its city/province, GSIN/UNSPSC and descriptions, procurement category, procurement method, selection criteria, trade agreements, regions of opportunity and delivery, expected contract start/end dates, and the closing date (documented UTC-0500) which with publicationDate gives the posting duration.
prediction_time: The instant is the original tender notice's publicationDate (the row with amendmentNumber 000; amendment rows are separate later publication events and are excluded from features and from the instant). Every shipped feature is a field of the notice as published at T, each documented in the publisher's own XML data dictionary (fetched 2026-10-31, 60,478 bytes). The label is a later state change of the same notice: the publisher's data dictionary defines tenderStatus as 'A status that indicates whether a tender is Open (ie: accepting bids), Expired (no longer accepting bids) or Cancelled', and the publisher's support page states the files 'will include information on new, open, cancelled and expired notices that are published on the CanadaBuys website' and that 'Tender notice closing times will be displayed in Universal Time Coordinated minus 5 hours (UTC-0500)'. As-of policy: the open-data files re-state the CURRENT status of each notice (the complete file carries live Open rows; the closed-FY files carry only terminal statuses - measured FY2023-24 file: 6,414 Expired / 415 Cancelled, zero Open). Historical cancellation DATES are not published in the bulk files, so labels are read as terminal states from an archive snapshot pinned by sha256 at harvest; still-Open solicitations are censored (excluded, not imputed). Cancellation is operationally observable in real time on the CanadaBuys site and the files refresh at least daily (2026-2027 tender file Last-Modified measured Sat, 31 Oct 2026 10:30:31 GMT). Residual limitation, recorded not resolved: rare late reversions of already-published statuses cannot be excluded for the most recent window; construction runs a bounded notice-page verification on a sample of Cancelled rows.
target_definition: Binary: 1 if the solicitation's terminal tenderStatus (current archive) is 'Cancelled'; 0 if 'Expired'. Label source column: tenderStatus-appelOffresStatut-eng/-fra, excluded from shipped features. Population restricted to the RFP-like notice types above; excluded: Request for Information (measured 3.2% award-notice rate - no award by design), Advance Contract Award Notice (award pre-decided), Directed Contract and Not Applicable (non-competitive instruments). Observed absence vs no-event: 'Expired' is an observed terminal state (closed without cancellation), not missing data. Multi-row rule: 499/6,829 FY2023-24 solicitations carry amendment rows with their own later publication dates, and 144 of those show differing statuses across rows - construction defines precedence as any-row-Cancelled (solicitation-level label), verified on a bounded sample against the notice pages; measured FY2023-24 impact of the precedence choice is small (base rate 6.08% under max-amendment-row vs 6.1-6.9% band). Censoring: solicitations still Open at harvest are excluded. Optional recorded variant (NOT the primary label): no award notice published among Expired RFP-like solicitations (measured ~48% in the FY2023-24 + FY2024-25 award files) - ambiguous because award-notice publication is not guaranteed for every award.

Measured basis (FY2023-24, whole-FY bounded sample): RFP-like population 5,749 solicitations with 397 Cancelled (6.90%); all-solicitations 6,829 with 415 Cancelled (6.08%); both classes present. Per-window exact counts are the FIRST construction measurement on the worker (the ~746 MB tender archive download is bulk work and stays off the coordinator); no sampled number is claimed as a total. measurements.schema_2026_10_31: 67 columns, bilingual eng/fra, identical header in the FY files, the complete file and the 2009-2022 legacy file (range-slice verified). Publisher data dictionary documents every column; key documented semantics quoted: tenderStatus ('Open (ie: accepting bids), Expired (no longer accepting bids) or Cancelled'); tenderClosingDate ('The date of closing for a tender notice, after which no new submissions will be accepted... displayed are all in UTC-0500... EASTERN STANDARD TIME'); amendmentNumber ('The number of amendments against a tender notice and/or a related awarded contract' - a running counter, so amendment counts on original rows are NOT as-of-T facts and are excluded from features); noticeType taxonomy (RFP, ACAN, ITQ, RFI, RFSO, RFSA, RFP against SA, Directed Contract, Not Applicable); procurementMethod taxonomy (competitive open bidding / selective tendering / traditional, non-competitive, ACAN, limited tendering); selectionCriteria taxonomy; GSIN/UNSPSC + descriptions; regionsOfOpportunity/Delivery; contracting entity + end-user entity fields; expectedContractStart/EndDate; tradeAgreements; noticeURL; tenderDescription (full text).

review: Five contracts at probe time: (1) Redistribution - SUPPORTED: OGL-Canada 2.0, explicit copy/modify/publish/adapt/distribute grant incl. commercial use, attribution statement required and carried to LICENSE.md; class A. (2) Prediction timing - SUPPORTED with recorded limitation: instant = original-notice publicationDate; every shipped feature is an original-notice field documented in the publisher's own data dictionary; the label is a post-instant terminal state from the publisher's own refreshed archive; cancellation dates are not in the bulk data, so the as-of policy is pinned-archive terminal-state with Open-row censoring + bounded notice-page verification at construction (weaker than dated-event labels like austender's; recorded as such). (3) Target - SUPPORTED: tenderStatus is a publisher-maintained column with documented three-value semantics; 'Expired' is observed absence (closed normally), 'Cancelled' the event; label column excludable; eligibility defined from information at the instant (notice type, competitive methods) not from outcomes. (4) Split capacity - PARTIALLY MEASURED: whole-FY2023-24 measured (5,749 eligible, 397 positives, 6.90%); legacy archive measured to carry the label across 2012-2022 via bounded slices; per-window exact counts need one bulk worker pass (recorded as the prerequisite to ready; never extrapolated to a claimed total). (5) Not a mirror - differentiated (novelty check recorded): no ML-ready cancellation task for any jurisdiction found; EU TED outcome-prediction literature studies different targets on a different jurisdiction and is not shipped ML-ready; the nearest bench sibling austender-contract-amendment-occurrence is the same domain but a different task contract (post-award contract amendments vs pre-award solicitation cancellation; different instant, population and label source).
next_action: One bounded worker measurement pass (advancement owns it), then ready/drop decision on measured criteria. Job: download tender complete (188,290,269 B) + tender legacy (558,413,231 B) + award complete (104,817,598 B), sha256-pin each, build the per-solicitation frame (earliest-publication row = features; any-row-Cancelled = terminal status; RFP-like notice types only; censor still-Open), and compute per-year eligible counts, cancellation rates and the three disjoint window counts (indicative windows train 2009-2019 / eval 2020-2023 / holdout 2024-2026) with clustered counts on (contracting entity, publication-month). ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA to flip ready: every window carries both classes with >=100 clustered positives and a cancellation rate inside a 2-20% band (measured FY2023-24: 6.90%), the precedence rule verified against >=30 notice pages with >=95% agreement, and the provenance mix per window recorded. FAILURE MODE to record instead: any window without both classes, or a >2x rate discontinuity across the 2022-08 CanadaBuys migration boundary that cannot be handled by era-separate splits. If ready: construction step = the same worker job extends to the full artifact build (features from the original-notice row, description text shipped, status and amendment fields excluded), expected artifact = train/eval/holdout CSVs + quality.json under the repository's construction path, decided by the standard gate.
